summary: Discovery with Mosaic Retail to scope model selection and deployment mode. Customer focused on multilingual support, long context (up to 64k tokens for session logs), tool-calling for inventory/price lookups, and data residency for EU customers. Discussed tradeoffs between Redwood Hosted (fast to start), Dedicated (predictable throughput/cost), and Private (VPC/on-prem with KMS) for regulated payments/PII. Agreed to Hosted eval and deeper technical deep-dive for on-prem network topology and KV-cache implications.
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-09-17
Time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Devon Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (CTO - Mosaic), Samir Kapoor (Head of ML), Jules Park (SRE), Evelyn Tran (Product)

SUMMARY SECTION (auto):
- Quick scoping: target features (customer support agents, personalized recommendations, in-app search)
- Primary technical asks: support for 64k context, multilingual (EN/ES/FR), tool-calling for inventory and pricing, and EU data residency
- Operational asks: SLA, reserved capacity pricing, SOC2 + KMS, and rollout plan

[00:00] Ava Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — quick intros then we can jump into context and constraints.
[00:20] Lena Ortiz: Hi Ava, thanks. I'll kick it off — Mosaic supports 8 markets, lots of Spanish and French content, and we have session logs that can be pretty long, sometimes 30k to 60k tokens when you include conversation + product history.
[00:35] Samir Kapoor: Yup, our use cases are twofold: customer support assistance where agent and chat history matter, and a recommendations microservice that uses tool-calling to query live inventory and prices.
[00:50] Devon Patel: Great, that frames it. When you say 30k-60k tokens, is that per user session, or aggregated across threads?
[01:05] Jules Park: Per session—like when an agent has a full chat log plus the customer's order history, it's large. We can truncate but quality drops.
[01:20] Speaker 1: And we want to avoid sending PII out of EU regions, that's a hard constraint for a subset of our customers.
[01:35] Ava Chen: Understood. Quick high-level on options: Redwood Hosted gets you running fastest, Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and cost, Private (VPC / on-prem) handles strict data residency and KMS. Each has different tradeoffs for latency and cost with long-context workloads.
[01:55] Lena Ortiz: What's the practical limit for context on Hosted? I saw references to 32k models but we need 64k for some flows.
[02:10] Devon Patel: Good question — we onboard a few 64k-capable open models (we often evaluate Mistral, Llama variants, and our own tuned ensembles). Hosted can run 64k models but needs different kernel paths and memory—latency will increase. Dedicated lets you pin GPU types and batch windows to manage latency. Private gives you the most control but comes with infra setup time.
[02:40] Samir Kapoor: You mentioned ensembles — are you talking about model fallback or routing?
[02:48] Devon Patel: Both. For example, route short queries to a cheaper 7B quantized variant, and long-history flows to a 32k/64k variant. Also automated fallback to a slightly older quantized checkpoint if load spikes.
[03:05] Evelyn Tran: On multilingual quality, we've seen big differences between models — do you have benchmarks for Spanish/French?
[03:15] Ava Chen: We do. We'll send a short report, but high-level: some open models maintain strong English performance but degrade on technical Spanish. For retail conversational tasks we recommend a fine-tuned or instruction-tuned checkpoint; Redwood Optimize can recommend a quantization/profile that balances token cost and quality.
[03:40] Lena Ortiz: How does tool-calling work with long contexts? For us, tool calls must be deterministic and low-latency — inventory and price lookups should not add more than 100-150ms.
[03:55] Devon Patel: Tool-calling is handled as synchronous external calls triggered by model output (function calling). The runtime isolates tool serialization and we can pin those requests on low-latency routing policies. For Dedicated pools you can co-locate service endpoints or create a fast private network to minimize RTT.
[04:20] Samir Kapoor: What's the standard approach to caching product lookups? We don't want to call inventory every time.
[04:30] Jules Park: We're already using CDN-level caching for static product metadata, but inventory is dynamic.
[04:36] Devon Patel: Redwood supports prefix/KV caching for model contexts — for tool results you can use an application cache or Redwood-provided short-lived artifact cache. We can tune TTLs; also batch multiple tool calls where appropriate.
[04:50] Speaker 2: Quick — any gotchas with quantization for multilingual models?
[04:55] Devon Patel: Slight risk: extreme quantization (4-bit) can hurt linguistic nuance in low-resource languages. We usually recommend mixed strategies: quantize inference weights but keep key layers in higher precision, or run a small ensemble for languages where lower precision hurts.
[05:15] Lena Ortiz: Security is big. SOC2 and KMS integration — if we go Dedicated, will our keys be customer-managed?
[05:25] Ava Chen: Yes for Private and Dedicated we can integrate with customer KMS/HSM. Hosted can support customer-managed keys depending on contract (we'll include in the security playbook). We'll send SOC2 + whitepaper.
[05:40] Samir Kapoor: Data residency — some EU sessions must never leave EU. How do you ensure that?
[05:48] Devon Patel: We can pin routing by region and restrict model variants to certain regions. Private on-prem is the strictest, but Hosted with EU region and Dedicated regional pools also work. Audit logs and access controls are available for all modes.
[06:05] Evelyn Tran: Cost — can you ballpark token cost difference between Hosted and Dedicated for a long-context 64k session?
[06:15] Ava Chen: Ballpark only: Hosted is often higher per-token for premium throughput but lower operational overhead up-front. Dedicated with reserved capacity reduces unit cost by committing and optimizing batching — for heavy long-context workloads Dedicated is usually more economical. We'll provide an estimate after we see your token distribution.
[06:35] Lena Ortiz: Let's talk about evals. Samir has a labeled test set for Spanish customer queries and a few thousand dialogues for long-context scoring. We want Rouge-like and response-quality metrics.
[06:50] Samir Kapoor: Yes we'll share that. Also want to test hallucination rates when tool-calling fails.
[06:58] Devon Patel: Makes sense. Our eval harness can run hallucination/regression alerts tied to the prompt set. We can run an A/B between model variants and also test function-call failure modes.
[07:15] Speaker 1: Are there any existing customers in retail doing this scale?
[07:20] Ava Chen: Yes, a few mid-market retail customers run 32k contexts in Dedicated. 64k is newer but we're running pilots with partners.
[07:30] Lena Ortiz: Operationally, how long to stand up Dedicated? We have a Q4 launch target for an initial pilot.
[07:40] Ava Chen: Dedicated typically takes 2–6 weeks depending on capacity and contract; Private on-prem takes longer (6–12 weeks) because of network/topology and KMS setup. Hosted is immediate. For Q4 pilot, Hosted eval start now and plan Dedicated procurement in parallel.
[07:58] Jules Park: Network requirements — if Dedicated is in our VPC peering setup, what ports and throughput?
[08:06] Devon Patel: We'll provide a network playbook. Generally you need stable egress, and cgroup-like throughput for model RPCs. If peering, TCP+gRPC on specific ports; we'll share exact firewall and bandwidth guidelines.
[08:25] Samir Kapoor: Tool-calling reliability — is there built-in retry or circuit breaking?
[08:31] Devon Patel: Yes, runtime-level retries and fallback policies exist. Also you can configure automatic fallback to cached tool results or to a degraded mode (e.g., 'sorry I can't fetch that right now') and log the event.
[08:45] Evelyn Tran: For multilingual fine-tuning, do you support customer-provided instruction tuning?
[08:52] Ava Chen: Absolutely — we help onboard fine-tuning data and can run a managed fine-tune on Dedicated hardware. For Hosted there's a managed tuning flow. We'll note that training data residency must be considered.
[09:10] Speaker 3: Any known gotchas with LLM function calling and idempotency for inventory updates?
[09:17] Devon Patel: Model outputs are non-deterministic; we recommend using function-calling with strong schema validation and idempotency tokens on the backend, plus a lightweight middleware to dedupe.
[09:32] Samir Kapoor: We want to run a benchmark: 5000 simulated sessions with 25% long-context >40k, 50% tool calls. Can Redwood run that on Dedicated emulation?
[09:43] Devon Patel: Yes, we can run load tests. We'll need your prompt set and traffic profile. We'll include KV-cache hit-rate assumptions in the plan.
[09:55] Ava Chen: Next steps recap — we'll send Dedicated pricing, security docs, and a benchmark plan. You'll share labeled eval sets and latency targets. We'll provision a Hosted eval and schedule a technical deep-dive.
[10:12] Lena Ortiz: Sounds good. One quick question — do you support realtime streaming while the model consults the KV cache, or do you buffer?
[10:20] Devon Patel: We stream tokens as they are generated; KV cache lookups are integrated into generation so you'll see a small hit but tokens stream continuously. For very large KV lookups we might stream partial results and flush.
[10:40] Samir Kapoor: On monitoring — can we get per-token cost breakdown and per-route latency metrics?
[10:45] Ava Chen: Yes Redwood Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns per model and per route, and you can drill to token-level traces. We'll give a demo in the deep-dive.
[11:00] Jules Park: Any regulatory concerns for storing logs for 12 months? We need audit logs and retention controls.
[11:08] Ava Chen: Audit logs and retention policies are configurable; for Private you control retention entirely. For Hosted/Dedicated we offer retention controls and can sign a DPA.
[11:25] Speaker 2: If we move to Dedicated, how are upgrades handled — can we do canary rollouts?
[11:32] Devon Patel: Yes, rollouts, canaries, and A/Bs are part of the platform. You can pin traffic percentages and have automatic fallback rules.
[11:45] Evelyn Tran: What's the usual performance delta between quantized 7B and 32k 30B variants for our tasks?
[11:53] Devon Patel: Huge delta in latency and cost — 7B quantized is much cheaper and faster but may miss long-range dependencies. 30B 32k models are slower/higher cost but better at preserving long-context coherence. We'll map this to your eval results.
[12:15] Lena Ortiz: For the Hosted eval, can we test both Spanish and French sets?
[12:20] Ava Chen: Yes — include the sets when you share the eval artifacts. We'll run both.
[12:30] Samir Kapoor: Regarding tool calls, can we simulate degraded downstream (DB timeouts) and measure hallucination or compensating behaviour?
[12:38] Devon Patel: Yes, the eval harness can inject faults and test fallback policies.
[12:50] Speaker 1: Anything else we should know before we wrap?
[12:55] Jules Park: Timeline — we want eval results within two weeks if possible.
[13:00] Ava Chen: We'll aim for that; Devon will own the benchmark plan.
[13:07] Samir Kapoor: Great, thanks.

(Several minutes of side conversation and minor clarifications omitted for brevity; call continues with detailed gating questions)

[35:00] Devon Patel: Quick note on KV cache architecture: our KV is sharded and uses a memory-first cache with optional SSD spillover. For 64k sessions you want more memory to avoid SSD thrash. That affects Dedicated sizing.
[36:10] Lena Ortiz: What's a recommended GPU type for 64k runs?
[36:18] Devon Patel: For 64k you typically want A100 80GB-class or next-gen with large VRAM; some customers use multi-GPU with KV-aware split. We can recommend exact instance types in the sizing doc.
[37:00] Samir Kapoor: If we do multi-region, can we replicate KV cache while keeping EU-only data separate?
[37:08] Devon Patel: Yes — policy-based routing and selective replication. EU PII can be kept in region and non-PII replicated.
[38:00] Ava Chen: Ok, wrapping — we'll produce the docs and benchmark plan. Any blockers?
[38:12] Lena Ortiz: No blockers. We'll get the eval sets and latency SLOs by tomorrow.
[38:20] Ava Chen: Perfect, thanks all.

End of recording.
